title: Best Piano Teacher Software (2026): 7 Tools Compared
description: Piano teacher software compared on published prices and piano studio needs: practice tracking, repertoire, makeup credits, recitals and sheet music.
body:
Most piano teachers run a one-person studio: a few dozen weekly students, mostly kids, with parents paying monthly tuition and asking what to practice. Generic booking apps cover the calendar and the invoice. The piano-specific jobs are practice between lessons, tracking which pieces each student is on, makeup lessons and recitals, and only some music lesson tools do them. We checked seven tools that sell to independent music teachers against those jobs, using only each vendor's own public pages, checked on November 19, 2026. If a vendor doesn't publish something, we say "not listed" or "unknown". We haven't used these tools ourselves and we don't publish ratings.

{{table:trio,nova-music,tutortally,duet,mysymphony,my-music-staff,fons}}

Which one fits

  • You want students to practice, and you want proof: Trio lists the most practice tools: daily targets, streaks, video clips students send mid-week and a weekly email to parents. Pro is $5/mo. Nova Music logs practice even on its free plan, but billing needs Pro at $10/mo. {{aff:trio|See Trio's plans}}
  • Your students use method books: MakeMusic Studio is the only tool here that lists a built-in music library, with titles from Alfred's Basic Piano Library and Suzuki and play-along accompaniment. It costs the most here at $19.95/mo, and it publishes its card and ACH fees. It doesn't say which Alfred levels or books are included. {{aff:fons|See MakeMusic Studio}}
  • Makeup lessons are your biggest headache: My Music Staff, Trio and Nova Music Pro all list makeup credits. My Music Staff ($16.95/mo) also tracks repertoire per student and builds you a studio website.
  • You run a spring recital: Trio lists recital running order, RSVPs and printed programs, and lets you bill a recurring recital fee. mySymphony lists recital tracking on its Ensemble plan ($15/mo for the first teacher).
  • You teach part-time: mySymphony Solo charges only for lessons you book ($0.25 each, never more than $20/mo). TutorTally is $59.99 once if you'd rather not pay monthly, but it only runs on iPhone, iPad and Mac, and families pay you directly.
  • You only have a handful of students: Trio Free and Nova Music Free cover up to 10 students. See our free music lesson software guide for what each free plan leaves out.

Hiring a second teacher later? Per-teacher costs vary: My Music Staff and MakeMusic Studio add $4.95/mo per teacher, Trio adds $5/mo per seat, and Nova Music's multi-teacher plan is listed as coming soon. Our best music lesson studio software page covers multi-teacher studios.

What we couldn't confirm

Which Trio plan includes the practice, repertoire and recital tools (the feature list doesn't say); whether mySymphony's PDF play-along needs the "Symphony tier" its home page mentions, since its pricing page lists only Solo, Ensemble and add-ons; payment processing rates for Trio, Nova Music, mySymphony and My Music Staff; annual prices for My Music Staff, MakeMusic Studio and mySymphony; and whether Duet is still actively developed (its pricing page still shows 2024 promotions). Before you switch, export your student list and lesson history and run a month of real lessons on a free trial. Our software buying checklist lists what to ask, and My Music Staff alternatives covers moving off My Music Staff.

faq: What is the cheapest software for a piano teacher?

Trio and Nova Music are free for up to 10 students. TutorTally is free for 2 students, then $4.99/mo, $29.99/yr or $59.99 once. Beyond 10 students, Trio Pro is $5/mo (or $50/yr) with no student limit (vendor pricing pages, checked 2026-11-19).
Which piano teacher software tracks student practice?

Trio lists practice assignments with per-day targets, streaks and practice video uploads. Nova Music includes practice logging on its free plan. mySymphony sells a Student Practice Dashboard (metronome, tuner, practice tracking) as a $20/mo add-on. MakeMusic Studio includes play-along practice tools with tempo control and looping (vendor pages, checked 2026-11-19).
Does any studio software include piano method books?

MakeMusic Studio (formerly Fons) lists a built-in catalog with titles from Alfred's Basic Piano Library, Suzuki and Disney, included in its $19.95/mo subscription for teachers and students. It doesn't publish which specific books or levels are included (studio.makemusic.com, checked 2026-11-19).

My Music Staff lets you issue and use make-up credits. Trio lists makeup credits with a cancellation policy engine. Nova Music includes makeup credits on Pro ($10/mo). TutorTally lets you add makeup lessons by hand as one-off lessons (vendor pages, checked 2026-11-19).
Can piano teacher software manage a recital?

Trio lists events and recitals with running order, RSVPs and programs, plus recurring recital fees. mySymphony lists recital and performance event tracking on its Ensemble plan ($15/mo for the first teacher). We didn't find recital tools listed by the other tools here (vendor pages, checked 2026-11-19).
